'''Austin Stevens''' (born 19 May 1950) is a South African-born Australian<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://fishgame.com/2015/10/snakemaster-speaks-a-conversation-with-austin-stevens/|title=Snakemaster Speaks: A Conversation with Austin Stevens|date=2015-10-22|work=Texas Fish & Game Magazine|access-date=2017-11-14|language=en-US}}</ref> naturalist, [[herpetologist]], [[wildlife photographer]], documentarian, television personality, and author.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.austinstevens.net/|title=Austin Stevens - Snakeman, Herpetologist, Adventurer, Photographer, Filmmaker, Author|author=Admin}}</ref> He is best known as the host of the [[Animal Planet]] [[nature documentary]] series ''Austin Stevens: Snakemaster'' (2004−09).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://press.discovery.com/emea/wrld/programs/austin-stevens-most-dangerous/|title=Austin Stevens Most Dangerous : Programs : Discovery World : Discovery Press Web}}</ref>

==Early life==
{{BLP unsourced section|date=January 2021}}
Stevens was born on 19 May 1950 in [[Pretoria]], [[Transvaal Province|Transvaal]].  His mother was often ill, lost a lung in a car accident, and died when Stevens was in his 30s; his father owned a small typewriter repair business. Stevens became interested in [[snakes]] at the age of 12, and by the time he finished school, his reptile collection included some of the most exotic and venomous species in the world. He traces his adventurous streak back to his grandfather from [[Bristol]], England and part founder of the [[AJS|AJS Motorbike Corporation]].

==Career==
Stevens' career in herpetology also included hosting a TV programme called ''Austin Stevens: Snakemaster''. The show aired on [[Animal Planet]] in the United States and [[Five (channel)|5]] in the United Kingdom. For season two, the series was rechristened ''Austin Stevens Adventures'', which, in a similar vein to fellow Animal Planet shows ''[[The Crocodile Hunter]]'' and ''[[The Jeff Corwin Experience]]'', began focusing on other animals, such as [[rhino]]s and [[hyena]]s, along with snakes; the show was presented in [[High-definition television|high definition]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hd.net/affAustinStevens.html|title=新百合ヶ丘で整体をお探しなら！}}</ref> and broadcast a total of 28 episodes before ending in 2009. His book ''The Last Snake Man'' was published in the UK by Noir Publishing.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.noirpublishing.co.uk/wildlife.htm|title=Noir Publishing}}</ref>

Stevens uses a Samsung Pro815 and an unspecified Sony Cybershot model for general use.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ephotozine.com/article/ephotozine-talks-to-austin-stevens-13714|title=ePHOTOzine talks to Austin Stevens|author=Magezine Publishing Ltd|work=ePHOTOzine}}</ref>

===Personal life===
In December 2007, Austin Stevens married his second wife Amy, a young python keeper from [[Australia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/driving/features/article4176470.ece|title=Login}}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Following the marriage, Stevens relocated to Australia.

In September 2016, Stevens revealed that he had been diagnosed with [[Parkinson's disease]].<ref>{{cite web |url =https://www.facebook.com/AustinStevensAdventurer/photos/a.399023086803014.84856.396708543701135/1192692260769422/?type=3&theater|title= Austin Stevens - Adventurer Facebook post|website= [[Facebook]]|date= 5 September 2016|access-date= 14 October 2018}}</ref>

In June 2023, Stevens revealed that he had had surgery to remove a [[basal cell skin cancer]] from his right brow.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.facebook.com/AustinStevensAdventurer/posts/pfbid02ZeyrAeVvGBWQ3Le5BR2e3GcRsnSHaptD79NYrJyJRFSk1Jm3jXQS2Uuxx9SN3nzql | title= Austin Stevens - Adventurer Facebook post|website= [[Facebook]]|date= 13 June 2023|access-date= 16 June 2023}}</ref> Stevens later reported that the surgery was a success and no further treatment was necessary.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=800041441690207&set=pb.100050530747410.-2207520000. | title= Austin Stevens - Adventurer Facebook post|website= [[Facebook]]|date= 13 June 2023|access-date= 16 June 2023}}</ref>

==Works==
Some of his credits:
*''Dragons of the Namib'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.parthenonentertainment.com/programme.php?catid%3D1%26programmeid%3D89%26sectionid%3D2 |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2009-02-03 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110715050025/http://www.parthenonentertainment.com/programme.php?catid=1&programmeid=89&sectionid=2 |archivedate=15 July 2011}}</ref> a documentary about the life of the [[Namaqua Chameleon]]. Producer and cinematographer.
*''Africa's Deadliest Dozen'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://channel.nationalgeographic.com/channel/ET/popup/200610061100.html |title=National Geographic Channel TV Schedule - Africa's Deadly Dozen: Africa's Deadly Dozen &#91;TV-G&#93; |accessdate=2006-12-29 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20061129041345/http://channel.nationalgeographic.com/channel/ET/popup/200610061100.html |archivedate=29 November 2006}}</ref> a documentary about the venomous snakes of Africa. Cinematographer.
*Die Natur der Schlange (German: ''The Nature of Snakes''), a 1997 German Documentary on snakes, aired on [[ZDF]].
*Austin takes wildlife stock photographs for Animals Animals/Earth Scenes<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.animalsanimals.com/index.asp|title=Nature Stock Photography Agency Nature Photographs Stock Images Photos|author=MSH}}</ref>
*He is a media donor on [[ARKive]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arkive.org/donors/a3.html|title=Media donors - A|work=ARKive|access-date=30 December 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071228192640/http://www.arkive.org/donors/a3.html|archive-date=28 December 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Books:
*''Snakes in My Bed'' (Penguin 1992)
*''The Last Snake Man'' (Noir Publishing 2007) {{ISBN|978-0-9536564-6-2}}
*Snakemaster (Skyhorse Publishing 2014)
DVDs:
*''Snake Bite: In Search of the King Cobra'' (Go Entertain 2005)
*''Austin Stevens: Snakemaster'' (first three episodes)
